EventItemActionText:
The Board of Architectural Review met in a work session in Town Hall, 127 Center St. S., Vienna, Virginia, on Wednesday, April 22, 2026, at 8:00 a.m.
The following members were present: Ms. Hanley, Ms. Couchman, Ms. Shelley, and Mr. Penati.
Mr. O’Keefe was absent.
Staff present: Sharmaine Abaied, Planner and Patricia Taylor, Board Clerk.

Applicant/Representatives present: Leslie Herman (Parks and Recreation), Dave Donahue (Public Works), and Fred Hiser (WRA LLP).
Mr. Hiser reviewed the existing conditions of the amphitheater and presented proposed structural repairs and refinishing options. The discussion focused on deterioration of the wood columns at their base due to moisture exposure and the proposed solution to elevate the columns on concrete bases. 
The Board discussed the height and visual impact of the proposed concrete bases and questioned whether a reduced height or alternative approach could achieve the same structural benefit while improving aesthetics. The applicant indicated the height was based on structural recommendations and would evaluate whether adjustments are feasible.
The Board also discussed the extent of column replacement, with staff noting that only the most deteriorated columns would be replaced while others would be retained and repaired.
Color schemes and material options for refinishing the structure were presented. The Board indicated general support for the proposed color direction and materials.
Additional discussion included the potential modification or removal of non-structural elements and the importance of maintaining consistency with the overall design of the Town Green.
After discussion, the Board recommended the following:
This is the follow up for the amphitheater:
 
After discussion, the Board recommended the following:

•             Bring the wood column up and use Simpson base plates / post bases.
•             Preserve the natural look (Cedar) and keep the truss plates black.
•             Contrasting shed colors, darker but not red.
•             Investigate stormwater mitigation.
•             Future application requires an updated drawing.
